newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end topsy-turvy day mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end topsy-turvy day mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished a topsy-turvy day slightly higher, with Standard & Poor 500s caught in end-of-quarter cross currents, traders and analysts said.

They said the choppy market action, stemming from the end of quarter position-squaring, would continue for the next week, and possibly jostle December back to the low 690.00s before lifting the contract to record highs.
"There will be a lot of money that will be put to work at the 690.00 area," one floor trader who handles institutional business said.
December S&Ps fell through 690.00 this morning on aggressive dealer selling. Speculation of asset allocation into bonds, from stocks, dissipated later in the session.

Morgan Stanley's global strategist, Barton Biggs, said he believes the U.S. stock market could rally five to 10 percent in ythe short-term. And soon after midday, the Investment Company Institute (ICI) said about $17.93 billion in net new cash flowed into stock mutual funds in August.
In fact, traders determined that the cash and futures S&P markets were starting to dovetail with the bond market after several weeks of diverging price patterns.

"The only reason we didn't rally from the five-year note auction is because the pit was already so long," one floor trader said about the positive results of the Treasury Department's five-year note aution.
U.S. bond futures rose slightly after the sale produced an average yield of 6.409 percent, in line with trade forecasts.
By that time, the December S&P contract had already rallied to 646.40, slightly above a 21-month bullish trendline, they said. Earlier in the day, the contract had stalled at 695.80.
Fair value for December S&Ps is at 5.65 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 6.40 points and arbitrage sell programs at 4.95 points.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were up 0.90 at 691.95, New Composites were up 0.95 at 368.55, KBT Value lines were up 0.30 at 640.70, Nikkeis were 100.0 points higher at 21,575, Midcap 400s were up 1.55 at 243.50, and Nasdaq 100s were down 0.60 at 753.40.
